title: Chloroform-Methanol Protein Extraction with Bead Beating for Yeast
author: Leanne Chan
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.btj3nkqn
materials: Chemicals to prepare: • Prepare 100 millimolar (mM), Tris(2-carboxyethyl)phosphine (TCEP) solution by dissolving 28.7 mg, TCEP in 1 mL, 100mM Ammonium Bicarbonate • Prepare 200 millimolar (mM), Iodoacetamide (IAA) solution by dissolving 36.8 mg, Iodoacetamide in 1 mL, 100mM Ammonium Bicarbonate •Prepare 1 mg/mL, Trypsin by adding 1 mL, 1mM HCl to 1 mg, Trypsin Store TCEP, IAA, and Trypsin in -20C. IAA is light sensitive. Store in amber tube (Fisher Scientific, Cat.#05-402-31).
Carefully pipet out clear liquid sample into plastic autosampler vials (ThermoFisherScientific, Cat.#03-060-016) or a 96-well plate (BIO-RAD, Cat.#HSP9601).

steps.title: Thaw cells
steps.instruction: Thaw frozen yeast cells at room temperature. Omit this step if cells are taken directly from active cultures.

steps.title: Transfer cells to tubes
steps.instruction: Aliquot 2–4 OD·mL of cells into 8‑strip PCR tubes (Axygen Cat.#14‑222‑251) or a 96‑well PCR plate (ThermoFisher Cat.#AB0600). A tube filled 30–40 % (≈10–20 OD·mL) is appropriate.

steps.title: Add beads
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL of 0.5 mm Zirconia/Silica beads (BioSpec) to each tube. (Beads may be pre‑loaded before adding cells.)

steps.title: Bead beat cells
steps.instruction: Place tubes in a TissueLyser and run 5 cycles of 1 min at 30 Hz, with 30 s on ice between cycles.

steps.title: Collect liquid
steps.instruction: Gently spin the tubes to bring all liquid to the bottom, then transfer as much supernatant as possible into new PCR tubes.

steps.title: Add chloroform
steps.instruction: Add 60 µL chloroform (Sigma‑Aldrich Cat.#34854) to each tube, pipet/vortex to mix. Perform in a fume hood.

steps.title: Add methanol
steps.instruction: Add 60 µL LC‑MS grade methanol (VWR Cat.#BJLC230‑2.5) to each tube and pipet to resuspend. (Alternatively add 120 µL of a 1:1 methanol:chloroform mixture.)

steps.title: Add water
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL LC‑MS grade water (VWR Cat.#BJLC365‑2.5), pipet/vortex to mix. This creates an approximate 1:1:1 methanol:chloroform:water ratio, ~150 µL total volume.

steps.title: First centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 4000 rpm, 25 °C for 1 minute.

steps.title: Remove aqueous layer
steps.instruction: Carefully pipette off the top layer (methanol + water) without disturbing the lower phase.

steps.title: Add methanol to pellet
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL methanol; break up the protein pellet with the pipet tip and direct methanol to the bottom of the tube.

steps.title: Second centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 4000 rpm, 25 °C for 2 minutes.

steps.title: Discard solvents
steps.instruction: Carefully discard the methanol + chloroform solvent into appropriate halogenated‑solvent waste.

steps.title: Air‑dry pellet
steps.instruction: Air‑dry the pellet for 5 minutes in a fume hood. Do not exceed 45 minutes, or the pellet will be difficult to resuspend.

steps.title: Resuspend pellet
steps.instruction: Resuspend the dried pellet in 60 µL 100 mM ammonium bicarbonate containing 20 % methanol. The suspension will appear cloudy.

steps.title: Store until assay
steps.instruction: Store the resuspended samples at –20 °C until ready for protein quantitation.

steps.title: Dilute samples ten‑fold
steps.instruction: Add 5 µL of protein sample to 45 µL water in a PCR tube or plate (final volume 50 µL) and mix well immediately before the assay.

steps.title: Prepare assay plate
steps.instruction: Transfer two replicates of each sample, 5 µL water (blank), and 5 µL Pierce BSA standard (ThermoFisher Cat.#23208) into a Corning 96‑well black plate (Fisher Scientific Cat.#07‑200‑590).

steps.title: Add Reagent A
steps.instruction: Add 25 µL Bio‑Rad DC Protein Assay Reagent A (Cat.#500‑0113) to each well and incubate for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Add Reagent B
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL Bio‑Rad DC Protein Assay Reagent B (Cat.#500‑0114) to each well and incubate for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Read absorbance
steps.instruction: Measure absorbance at 280 nm with a microplate reader and calculate protein concentrations.

steps.title: Adjust protein concentration
steps.instruction: Dilute protein samples to 2.4 µg/µL in 100 mM ammonium bicarbonate (AMBIC); mix well before proceeding.

steps.title: Prepare digestion mix
steps.instruction: Combine protein, TCEP, IAA, and trypsin in 100 mM AMBIC to reach final concentrations of 2 µg/µL protein (in 50 µL total), 5 mM TCEP, 10 mM IAA, and 2 µL trypsin (1 mg/mL, 1:50 ratio). Use one of the following volume schemes:

substeps.instruction: If protein stock is 2.4 µg/µL: add 41.67 µL protein, 2.5 µL TCEP (100 mM), 2.5 µL IAA (200 mM), 2 µL trypsin (1 mg/mL), then add AMBIC up to 50 µL total.
If protein stock is insufficient (≈1 µg/µL): add 20.83 µL protein, 2.5 µL TCEP (100 mM), 2.5 µL IAA (200 mM), 1 µL trypsin (1 mg/mL), then add AMBIC up to 50 µL total.

steps.title: Digest proteins
steps.instruction: Incubate the digestion mixture at 37 °C for 4 – 16 hours.

steps.title: Post‑digestion spin
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 4000 rpm, 4 °C for 15 minutes to pellet any debris.

steps.title: Final storage
steps.instruction: Store the cleared digest at –20 °C until LC‑MS/MS analysis.
